items.title: A map that is injective and unramified at a prime is etale after a principal localization, over a geometrically unibranch domain
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement assumes a domain as base, geometric unibranchness at the prime, unramifiedness of the map at the prime and injectivity of the localized map, and concludes that the map becomes etale after inverting one element outside the prime (statement lines 31762-31774). The proof first replaces the map by a standard etale cover with a surjection onto the given ring, then carries out a reduction to the case where that cover is a domain: it uses that the cover is reduced, that its fibre over the generic point is a finite product of fields so the minimal primes lie over the generic point, that a small number of them exist, and that geometric unibranchness makes the localization of an etale algebra at a prime a domain, after which an element separating the minimal primes produces the reduction (proof lines 31776-31797). The final step is a contradiction argument that invokes the previous lemma on ideals meeting the source domain, which is precisely why injectivity at the prime enters (proof lines 31799-31814). The counted span refers seven times, three times to results of this chapter and four times to other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
